scope: Research only; no checkout source edits and no media downloads. Eleven unique proposed YouTube IDs for natural-light, first-edit and teaching starters.

verification.identityAndEmbed: For every selected ID, the official YouTube oEmbed endpoint returned the credited title, channel and an iframe. This confirms supported public embed metadata, not end-to-end playback in Framepath or availability in every region.
verification.duration: Full durations were read from lengthSeconds in public YouTube watch-page metadata.
verification.captions: captionTracksFound means YouTube's page contained caption-track metadata. Languages, accuracy and live caption rendering were not checked. A false result is unknown availability, not proof that no captions exist.
verification.timing: Excerpts use the creator's published chapter boundaries or the complete duration of a short video. No topic timestamps are invented.
verification.duplicates: No selected ID matched app, lib, docs, tests, scripts, CURRICULUM.md or public/templates in the Framepath checkout. Used --no-ignore because the checkout's ignore context otherwise hid app matches. Also checked the parent-provided used-ID list.
verification.ownerReview: Review actual playback and lesson fit before treating these as watched/visually verified. The teaching starter 1 clip is a candidate with a particularly explicit content-fit limitation below. Software demonstrations are examples; learners should use their existing editor.

videos.title: How to Use Window Lighting | Portrait Photography
videos.creator: Howcast · Joe Sinnott
videos.timingEvidence: Complete short video; official YouTube duration is 100 seconds.
videos.purpose: Find indirect window light, position the subject and use a household reflector. A 1:40 viewing fits inside an eight-minute tryout.
videos.fitLimit: Portrait photography example. Framepath should explicitly transfer the position/light observation to a phone video and may use an object instead of a person.
videos.transcriptEvidence: Creator page publishes the full text. It covers avoiding direct sun through the window, bouncing light with household materials and checking the background.
videos.note: Complete 1:40 lesson. Photographing a portrait is the example; the window-light position also applies to phone video. The creator provides a written transcript.

videos.title: Hard Light vs Soft Light | Film Lighting Techniques
videos.creator: Creative Path Films
videos.timingEvidence: Official description: hard-light example begins 03:47, diffusion example 04:05, two softbox examples 04:29 and 04:47; bounced-light chapter begins 05:19.
videos.purpose: Compare shadow edges across hard light and diffused/soft sources using the demonstrated examples.
videos.fitLimit: Uses studio gear. Buying lights or softboxes is unnecessary: written teaching should apply the comparison to a window, curtain and object.
videos.note: Creator chapters compare hard light, diffusion and softboxes. For your practice, compare window light with and without a safe curtain; no lighting purchase is needed.

videos.title: How to Adjust Exposure for Videos on iPhone (tutorial)
videos.creator: Foxtecc
videos.timingEvidence: Official creator description: adjustment begins 00:46, locking begins 01:21, third-party apps begin 02:25.
videos.purpose: Manually adjust brightness and prevent exposure from changing during a take.
videos.fitLimit: iPhone example from 2023. The description establishes the brightness/lock controls, not specifically a highlight-clipping demonstration; retaining highlight texture must be taught in Framepath's own example.
videos.note: iPhone exposure adjustment and lock chapters. Controls differ across phones; use the equivalent brightness and lock controls if available.

videos.title: How To Use Window Lighting To Make Your Youtube Videos Look Better | Natural Lighting Tutorial
videos.creator: Andrew Kan
videos.timingEvidence: Official description: natural/window-light advantages and limitations chapter 04:24; next steps begins 06:06.
videos.purpose: Recognize the limitations of daylight when repeating shots and plan a repeatable setup.
videos.fitLimit: The selected chapter covers daylight limitations. The precise setup-note procedure is Framepath teaching, not a verified procedure in this excerpt.
videos.companionArticle: Creator's own Medium article discusses the same window-light setup; it is an article, not a verified verbatim transcript.
videos.note: Creator chapter on the advantages and limits of natural light. Record your own time, window, subject position and test image to help repeat the setup.

videos.title: CapCut App Video Editing Tutorial - COMPLETE Guide (2025)
videos.creator: Justin Brown · Primal Video
videos.timingEvidence: Official description: project creation 00:19; interface 01:22; format/aspect ratio begins 01:47. The official Primal Video page embeds this exact ID.
videos.purpose: Select source footage, make a new phone editing project and recognize the timeline before assembling three chosen shots.
videos.fitLimit: Three-shot exercise is Framepath's application. CapCut availability and controls vary by country/version; no installation or account is required for the learning objective if the learner has another editor.
videos.note: CapCut mobile project-creation and interface chapters, recorded in 2025. Apply the same selection decisions in an editor you already use.

videos.title: Microsoft Clipchamp: Rearrange Clips & Remove Gaps in Seconds
videos.creator: EdTech Hustle
videos.timingEvidence: Complete short video; official YouTube duration is 155 seconds.
videos.purpose: Reorder timeline clips and close accidental gaps, supporting the assembly/order lesson.
videos.fitLimit: Clipchamp desktop/browser interface. Teach the transferable drag/reorder/check-the-join action for learners working on a phone.
videos.note: Complete 2:35 Clipchamp tutorial from 2025. The example uses a desktop editor; the ordering and gap-check decisions apply to phone editors too.

videos.title: CapCut Video Editing Tutorial - COMPLETE Guide (2021)
videos.creator: Justin Brown · Primal Video
videos.timingEvidence: Official description: footage editing chapter begins 03:48; B-roll chapter begins 06:11.
videos.purpose: Remove unwanted footage, trim starts/ends and inspect cuts for clarity and pacing.
videos.fitLimit: Older 2021 mobile interface; concepts remain transferable but controls may have moved. Framepath should supply the reason for each cut rather than treating button use as the complete lesson.
videos.note: Creator's footage-editing chapter. This is a 2021 CapCut demonstration; controls may differ in your current editor.

videos.title: BEST Clipchamp Video Editing Tips and Tricks
videos.creator: Kevin Stratvert
videos.timingEvidence: Official description: automatic captions chapter 03:06; recording chapter begins 04:31.
videos.purpose: Introduce automatic captioning as the starting point for an accessible edit.
videos.fitLimit: Desktop/browser example from 2023. Caption error correction/readability and dialogue/music balance must be covered explicitly in the lesson's teaching alternative; exact inclusion of all those topics in this excerpt is not verified.
videos.note: Creator's auto-caption chapter in Clipchamp. Check every generated word and its timing; use the lesson's sound-balance example alongside this excerpt.

videos.title: iMovie App Tutorial - How To Edit Videos On iPhone & iPad (2023)!
videos.creator: Justin Brown · Primal Video
videos.timingEvidence: Official description: export chapter begins 18:44; portrait-video chapter begins 19:53. Official Primal Video guide matches the source title and export topic.
videos.purpose: Export a finished video from a phone editing app to a usable file.
videos.fitLimit: iPhone/iPad iMovie example from 2023. Exported-file playback checking is a Framepath task, not claimed as verified in this excerpt.
videos.note: iMovie mobile export chapter, recorded in 2023. After export, open the saved file and check the first frame, ending, sound and captions.

videos.title: Obtaining Informed Consent
videos.creator: WITNESS
videos.timingEvidence: Complete short video; official YouTube duration is 84 seconds. WITNESS's own library embeds this exact ID.
videos.purpose: Introduce informed consent before recording and sharing someone's image or account.
videos.fitLimit: Human-rights interview context, not a legal rule for all educational settings. Apply only the general consent principles to this adult/object-only practice; retain the instruction not to film children or real learner records.
videos.captionStatus: Unknown; no captionTracks field was found in this public watch-page response. Burned-in text was not visually checked.
videos.note: Complete 1:24 WITNESS consent lesson, originally made for interviews. Use an object or consenting adult for this practice and keep private educational records out of frame.

videos.title: Teacher Tips | Engaging Instructional Videos
videos.creator: Modern Classrooms Project · Toni Rose Deanon
videos.timingEvidence: Complete short video; official YouTube duration is 170 seconds. Creator website and YouTube description identify the same Toni Rose instructional-video tip.
videos.purpose: Offer a teacher's perspective on planning engaging instructional videos.
videos.fitLimit: OWNER REVIEW NEEDED: the primary description confirms intentional words/content and engagement. Specific coverage of chunking, demonstrations and learner checks is not yet verified. Do not claim the clip teaches all three. The accompanying Edutopia article by the organization's founders directly supports those lesson elements.
videos.note: Complete 2:50 teacher tip from Modern Classrooms Project. Use the lesson's separate objective–demonstration–learner-check plan to structure your own short teaching video.

rejectedOrUnused.reason: UAMS linked it as microlecture advice, but official oEmbed identifies a different Canvas viewer-engagement tutorial. Excluded rather than assuming the linked description was accurate.
